Rover positions: NASA/JPL-Caltech, the rover localizations behind NASA's "Where is the rover" maps (Curiosity route and stops, Perseverance route and stops), latest: Curiosity Mars day 5,082, Perseverance Mars day 2,022. Distance driven is NASA's odometry; height is the elevation of each stop. Ground: NASA Mars Trek mosaics, MRO HiRISE (NASA/JPL/University of Arizona) at Gale and MRO CTX (NASA/JPL/MSSS, USGS) at Jezero; black-and-white images, tinted here. Mars days are turned into Earth dates from the landing dates (Curiosity, Perseverance) with one Mars day = 1.0275 Earth days (NASA GISS Mars24), so dates can be off by a day. Between two recorded stops, the rover's progress is spread evenly over the days in between. Photos: NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS, public domain. · Highcharts.com
